subject: Re: Benchmark methodology and SLO qualification — EdgeFin
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rahul Shah <rahul@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the EdgeFin infra team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same scope for the benchmark run:

Summary of SLOs you shared:
- P95 latency for single-stream generation (streaming responses) <= 150 ms for 512-token prompts
- Sustained throughput: 500 requests/sec with 95% of requests meeting the latency SLO
- Target concurrency: up to 50 concurrent streams per model instance
- Streaming: low-latency chunked output required (first token <= 60 ms) and steady inter-token latency <= 20 ms
- Availability goal for production: 99.9% with graceful degradation to smaller model variants

What Redwood will bench and deliver:
- Reproducible benchmark run with the prompt set you provide (we'll align on categories and seeds)
- Measurement definitions (cold vs warm, how we count streaming first-token, p50/p95/p99, tail noise filtering)
- Hardware baseline (A100/4xA100 vs customer target region hardware) and quantization tradeoffs
- A short report with configuration, raw CSVs, and an actionable tuning checklist (batching/cache/quantization suggestions)

Next steps:
1) Please share your prompt set and any guarded prompts you want excluded.
2) Share the eval harness or allow us to run our harness against your test account; if you prefer, send a tarball of the harness and sample configs.
3) Confirm the hardware target (we suggested A100 x2 for parity) and whether we should test with int8 quantized model variants.

Deliverable timeline: once we have the prompt set & harness, we can run the baseline within 3 business days and deliver initial results in 5 business days.

Attachments: N/A — I'll follow up with a method template.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Rahul Shah <rahul@edgefin.com>

Date: 2026-11-13T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Performance SLOs & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming EdgeFin will move forward with the benchmark. Attaching what we have: prompt set v3, our eval harness snapshot, and a handful of previous latency samples for context.

Quick notes on the prompt set:
- 2k prompts total across three categories: short-form (<=64 tokens), mid (65-256), long (257-1024).
- For streaming tests focus on the mid group (our interactive product surface).
- We redacted any PII and removed production-sensitive prompts — the attached prompt CSV is safe for benchmarking.

Eval harness notes:
- Harness expects an environment with Docker + Python 3.10; we included a small README in the tarball.
- Seeded RNG (seed=42) for prompt ordering; harness supports replaying with different concurrency profiles (we usually test linear ramp and step tests).
- Previous runs used g4dn.xlarge in the cloud; production target will be A100 or similar.

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v3.csv; edgefin_eval_harness_v2.tar.gz; edgefin_latency_samples.csv

We'll need Redwood to:
- Confirm measurement definitions (how you compute first-token latency for streaming and how you treat partial failures).
- Provide a reproducible runner (Docker image or instructions) so we can run locally if needed.

Priya will be our internal PM — cc'd.

Thanks,
Rahul
Infra Lead, EdgeFin
rahul@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rahul Shah <rahul@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priya Bhatia <priya.b@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology — measurement defs & reproducibility

Great — got the files, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions so our report matches EdgeFin expectations and the results are reproducible for both teams:

Measurement definitions we propose (please confirm or edit):
- First-token latency (streaming): time from request accept to first byte of streamed payload. We will take per-request times and report p50/p95/p99. For transient network jitter, we'll report both raw and a filtered tail using the IQR method.
- Inter-token latency: median inter-token time over the streaming duration, reported as p50/p95.
- Warm vs cold: cold = first request to a freshly started runtime (no KV cache); warm = after 100 requests have warmed caches. We'll capture both.
- Throughput stability: measure RPS over 60s windows during sustained runs; report 95th percentile of windowed RPS.
- Error handling: partial failures (stream cut) count as errors; we will also capture partial-output rate and retry behavior.

Reproducibility steps we will include in the deliverable:
1) Exact Git commit + Docker image tag for the runner we used.
2) Hardware spec (instance type, GPU driver, CUDA/cuDNN versions).
3) Seeded prompt order and full prompt CSV used (we'll publish the exact file name).
4) Benchmark config (concurrency profile, batch sizes, quantization flags).
5) Raw CSVs for every run and the aggregation script used to produce p95/p99.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can EdgeFin share a small sample of production traffic (anonymized request-size distribution) so we can match realistic sequence-length mix?
- Confirm whether we should run quantized variants (int8) as part of the baseline or as a follow-up — quantization can affect inter-token latency in non-linear ways.

Internal note for Neha / Rishi: if EdgeFin provides the production distribution, let's run both warm + steady-state stress to capture cache benefits and degradation points. Also add a small canary that measures first-token tail under 50 concurrent streams.

If this looks good Rahul, we'll provision a runner and share a Docker tag. Targeting a baseline run on Monday once Docker/commit is confirmed.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
